text.tspan: Many technologies, including STATBELT, offer a shortcut that allows us to run the test without
computing the test statistic first, as we did in examples 5 and 6. STATBELT and similar apps will ask
you to input the hypotheses and the sample mean, standard deviation, and sample size, then will compute
the test statistic and P-Value for you. These are commonly called t-tests in technology menus.
To conduct a hypothesis test for a mean using STATBELT Utility and summarized data, follow the path:
Tests → Inference for Means → One sample → Hypothesis test (choose “Column data from the main
spreadsheet” if you have a column of raw data).
Under “Where is the data?” choose “Summarized data.” Type the sample mean, sample standard
deviation, and the sample size n.
Type the mean μ from the null hypothesis into “Hypothesized mean μ₀.”
Under “Type of test,” choose Left-tailed (<), Right-tailed (>), or Two-tailed (≠).
Type the significance level α. The results appear as soon as you type.
The output from STATBELT will include the test statistic, the degrees of freedom, and the P-Value.
